subject: selection of "good" probes in exon CDF's

messages.author: 9e88bf5547db06fc
messages.subject: selection of "good" probes in exon CDF's
parts:
Hello group,

I would like to use a cdf with the following properties:

1) Grouped by genes (not by exons or transcipts): we need all
the probes that hit a gene.
2) Include only the probes that are known to be expressed (or at
least, somebody found somewhere a EST or a Refseq transcript that
includes these probes).

As far as I know, Brainarray provides cdf's grouped by genes. However,
if some of the included probes hit the gene in a putative (and in fact
false) exon, these probes are included. Does anybody know of a
"curated by expression" cdf file (grouped by genes)?

If there is none, is it possible to combine the information of two cdf
files to remove the indexes of the probes in the cdf grouped by genes
that are not included in the probes grouped by Refseq?

Thanks,

Angel Rubio

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: selection of "good" probes in exon CDF's
parts:
Hi folks.

Sorry for the delay on replying to this one, I meant to comment on
this earlier.

There are a lot of questions on the BioC newsgroup lately about custom
CDFs and picking probes and so on. To have complete control, you
would probably want to be familiar with the exact information within
the CDF. To do this, use readCdf() from the 'affxparser' package on
your favourite CDF and take some time to understand the outputted list.

On 21/02/2009, at 10:32 PM, Angel wrote:

>
> Hi David,
>
> It could be quite interesting for me to have this scripts. Probably
> they will be useful for many people. Would you mind to post them?
> Best regards,
>
> Angel
>
> On Feb 21, 1:01 am, David Rosenberg <david.m.rosenb...@gmail.com>
> wrote:
>> While I don't know of any tools to do what you need, I have a
>> collection of
>> scripts I've used to modify and/or revise cdfs, particularlay w.r.t.
>> grouping. If you'd like, I'll send/post them.
>>
>> On Feb 20, 2009 1:01 PM, "Angel" <rubio.diaz.an...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>
>> Hello group,
>>
>> I would like to use a cdf with the following properties:
>>
>> 1) Grouped by genes (not by exons or transcipts): we need all
>> the probes that hit a gene.

Is there any reason specifically to have them grouped by genes? In a
lot of cases, this is useful information that will be useful to have
access to later on. In addition, when using an appropriate CDF (e.g.
grouped by genes and then by exons) with ExonRmaPlm(), you can fit the
probe level model using *all* probes for the gene (i.e. using
mergeGroups=TRUE) anyways.

>> 2) Include only the probes that are known to be expressed (or
>> at
>> least, somebody found somewhere a EST or a Refseq transcript that
>> includes these probes).
>>
>> As far as I know, Brainarray provides cdf's grouped by genes.
>> However,
>> if some of the included probes hit the gene in a putative (and in
>> fact
>> false) exon, these probes are included. Does anybody know of a
>> "curated by expression" cdf file (grouped by genes)?

As for the "curated by expression", I worry about doing that. Unless
you are studying a system that is very well studied, you may exclude
probes that have useful information. And, even some probes that are
low intensity (below some cutoff of log2 say) may give useful
information, but just appear low due to their probe characteristics
(number of GCs, etc).

Or, do you simply mean "curated by annotation"? If that is the case,
notice that there are several different CDFs available for each chip.
For the human exon array, Affy has divided their probes/probesets by
annotation according to "core" (RefSeqs and well annotated),
"extended" (ESTs) and "full" (predicted)":

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/affymetrix-defined-transcript-clusters

I mostly make use of the "core" CDF (i.e. probes to well annotated
exons) myself.

>> If there is none, is it possible to combine the information of two
>> cdf
>> files to remove the indexes of the probes in the cdf grouped by genes
>> that are not included in the probes grouped by Refseq?

There is nothing out-of-the-box that can do this (as far as I know).
But, if you are familiar with the list structure returned from
readCdf(), this will be in principle straightforward.

Hope that helps.
Mark
